arxiv-1712-09574.title: Guarded and Unguarded Iteration for Generalized Processes Thanks: Research supported by the DFG project A High Level Language for Monad-based Processes (GO 2161/1-2, SCHR 1118/8-2)
arxiv-1712-09574.creator: Sergey Goncharov \rsuper a, Lutz Schröder \rsuper b, Christoph Rauch \rsuper c, Maciej Piróg \rsuper d
arxiv-1712-09574.description: Abstract . Models of iterated computation, such as (completely) iterative monads, often depend on a notion of guardedness, which guarantees unique solvability of recursive equations and requires roughly that recursive calls happen only under certain guarding operations. On the other hand, many models of iteration do admit unguarded iteration.

arxiv-1810-04763.title: Recursion Schemes, the MSO Logic, and the 𝖴 \mathsf{U} quantifier Thanks: Work supported by the National Science Centre, Poland (grant no. 2016/22/E/ST6/00041).
arxiv-1810-04763.creator: Paweł Parys
arxiv-1810-04763.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Paweł Parys. We study the model-checking problem for recursion schemes: does the tree generated by a given higher-order recursion scheme satisfy a given logical sentence. The problem is known to be decidable for sentences of the MSO logic. We prove decidability for an extension of MSO in which we additionally have an unbounding quantifier 𝖴 \mathsf{U} , saying that a subformula is true for arbitrarily large finite sets.

arxiv-2107-10616.title: Bounds on Quantum Information Storage and Retrieval
arxiv-2107-10616.creator: Gia Dvali
arxiv-2107-10616.description: Abstract We present certain universal bounds on the capacity of quantum information storage and on the time scale of its retrieval for a generic quantum field theoretic system. The capacity, quantified by the microstate entropy, is bounded from above by the surface area of the object measured in units of a Goldstone decay constant.

arxiv-2210-06854.title: Gauge Invariance of the Thermal Conductivity in the Quantum Regime
arxiv-2210-06854.creator: Axel Hübner, Santiago Rigamonti, Claudia Draxl
arxiv-2210-06854.description: Abstract The widely used linear-response (LR) theory of thermal conduction in the quantum regime rests on the yet unproven assumption, that the thermal conductivity is invariant with respect to the gauge of the energy density of the system. This assumption manifests itself clearly in, e.g. , Hardy’s formulation of the heat-flux operator [Phys. Rev. 132 , 168 (1963)].

arxiv-2306-15388.title: On reachability categories, persistence, and commuting algebras of quivers
arxiv-2306-15388.creator: Luigi Caputi † \dagger, Henri Riihimäki ∗
arxiv-2306-15388.description: Abstract . For a finite quiver Q Q , we study the reachability category 𝐑𝐞𝐚𝐜𝐡 Q \mathbf{Reach}_{Q} . We investigate the properties of 𝐑𝐞𝐚𝐜𝐡 Q \mathbf{Reach}_{Q} from both a categorical and a topological viewpoint. In particular, we compare 𝐑𝐞𝐚𝐜𝐡 Q \mathbf{Reach}_{Q} with 𝐏𝐚𝐭𝐡 Q \mathbf{Path}_{Q} , the category freely generated by Q Q .

arxiv-2404-08181.title: Pay Attention to Your Neighbours: Training-Free Open-Vocabulary Semantic Segmentation
arxiv-2404-08181.creator: Jose Dolz Sina HajimiriIsmail Ben Ayed, Jose Dolz Sina Hajimiri ÉTS Montreal🖂 seyed-mohammadsina.hajimiri.1@etsmtl.net
arxiv-2404-08181.description: Abstract Despite the significant progress in deep learning for dense visual recognition problems, such as semantic segmentation, traditional methods are constrained by fixed class sets. Meanwhile, vision-language foundation models, such as CLIP, have showcased remarkable effectiveness in numerous zero-shot image-level tasks, owing to their robust generalizability.

arxiv-2409-01169.title: KDAR neutrino scattering for 12 C target via charged current and muon angular distribution
arxiv-2409-01169.creator: Chaeyun Lee, Kyungsik Kim, Myung-Ki Cheoun, Eunja Ha, Tatsushi Shima, Toshitaka Kajino
arxiv-2409-01169.description: Abstract We investigate the charged current (CC) scattering of muon neutrinos ( ν μ \nu_{\mu} ) off 12 C using an incident neutrino energy of E ν μ = E_{\nu_{\mu}}= 236 MeV, as produced in kaon decay-at-rest (KDAR). In this energy regime, both quasielastic (QE) scattering and inelastic processes occurring below the QE region contribute simultaneously.

pmc-10483845.title: Carbon nanotubes: a powerful bridge for conductivity and flexibility in electrochemical glucose sensors
pmc-10483845.creator: Tianyi Yuwen, Danting Shu, Hanyan Zou, Xinrui Yang, Shijun Wang, Shuheng Zhang, Qichen Liu, Xiangxiu Wang, Guixue Wang, Yuchan Zhang, Guangchao Zang
pmc-10483845.description: The utilization of nanomaterials in the biosensor field has garnered substantial attention in recent years. Initially, the emphasis was on enhancing the sensor current rather than material interactions. However, carbon nanotubes (CNTs) have gained prominence in glucose sensors due to their high aspect ratio, remarkable chemical stability, and notable optical and electronic attributes.

pmc-11401172.title: The infiltration characteristics of expansive soil considering fracture under wet-dry cycle conditions
pmc-11401172.creator: Ya Zhao, Hongri Zhang, Guiyao Wang, Yanqi Yang
pmc-11401172.description: Expansive soils exhibit a relatively low permeability coefficient when structurally intact, allowing for their treatment as a homogeneous medium in calculations. However, the susceptibility of the slope's shallow area to numerous primary and secondary cracks under the influence of wetting and drying cycles challenges this approach.

pmc-11651980.title: Optimizing prostate biopsy decision-making for patients with Prostate Imaging-Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS) ≥3 lesions: novel magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based nomograms
pmc-11651980.creator: Yanling Chen, Jinhua Lin, Wenxin Cao, Tiebao Meng, Jian Ling, Zhihua Wen, Lingmin Kong, Long Qian, Yan Guo, Weijing Zhang, Huanjun Wang
pmc-11651980.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundCurrent protocols endorse biopsies for men with Prostate Imaging-Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS v2.1) scores ≥3. However, the subjective nature of PI-RADS can lead to increased false positives and unnecessary biopsies. Synthetic magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), which quantifies multiple relaxation parameters, and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC), which is the most commonly used quantitative metric, have not yet been combined with a predictive tool.

pmc-12560357.title: Association of remdesivir treatment with long-term mortality after COVID-19 hospitalization
pmc-12560357.creator: Trisha Agarwal, Laurel E. Beaty, Nichole E. Carlson, Tellen D. Bennett, Lindsey E. Fish, David A. Mayer, Kyle C. Molina, Jennifer L. Peers, Brandon J. Webb, Mengli Xiao, Adit A. Ginde, Neil R. Aggarwal
pmc-12560357.description: BackgroundEffectiveness of remdesivir (RDV) treatment on short-term mortality and other outcomes has been well-studied, yet the impact of RDV on long-term outcomes is less well-known. The objective of this study was to determine if inpatient RDV use in survivors of COVID-19 hospitalization is associated with reduced mortality after discharge.

pmc-12620598.title: Cardiac Remodeling and Functional Alterations in Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction (HFpEF): An Echocardiographic Assessment at a Tertiary Hospital in Bangladesh
pmc-12620598.creator: Mohammad Walidur Rahman, Manzoor Mahmood, Dipal Krishna Adhikary, Chaudhury Meshkat Ahmed, Md. Harisul Hoque, Tanjima Parvin, Sajal Krishna Banerjee, Md. Fakhrul Islam Khaled
pmc-12620598.description: BackgroundHeart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a complex pathophysiological entity characterized by varying degrees of cardiac structural and functional changes. This study evaluated the prevalence and pattern of cardiac remodeling and functional alterations in an HFpEF cohort in Bangladesh.MethodsThis study was conducted among 50 hospitalized HFpEF patients from December 2017 to March 2019 at Bangladesh Medical University.

pmc-13470233.title: SNAI1 ablation alters integrin-mediated adhesion and endocytic fate
pmc-13470233.creator: Chrysoula Tsirigoti, Mohamad Moustafa Ali, Anita Morén, Staffan Johansson, Michael J. Munson, Carl-Henrik Heldin, Aristidis Moustakas, Dorival Mendes Rodrigues-Junior
pmc-13470233.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Transcription factor SNAI1 guides plasticity and invasiveness in cancer. Using a complete SNAI1 knockout in mesenchymal, triple-negative breast cancer cells, unbiased genome-wide transcriptomic analysis revealed a marked under-expression of integrin-based adhesion and endocytic components. Utilizing this knockout cell model, complementary breast cancer cell models and functional screening of multiple differentially expressed genes, we found that the pioneering transcription factor FOXA1, whose expression is repressed by SNAI1, associates with several key mediators of the cellular phenotype.

pmc-13583179.title: Evaluation of Ambient Air Particulate Matter, Urine Arsenic Levels and the Effect on Residents Health in an Artisanal Mining Community and an Incorporated Mining Community in Ghana From April 2024 to July 2024: A Cross‐Sectional Study
pmc-13583179.creator: Nafisa Akua Assan, Eric N. Y. Nyarko, Justice Kumi, Emmanuel K. Ofori, Alberta Dzifa Dayie, Derrick N. D. Doodo, Maxwell Seyram Sunu, Aliu Issahaku, Isaac Kpabitey Lawer, Christian Obirikorang, Henry Asare‐Anane
pmc-13583179.description: Background and AimOver 200 million people in developing and industrialized countries are exposed to arsenic poisoning. Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) constitutes a significant air contaminant, especially in urban and industrial suburbs. A significant proportion of countries do not possess sufficient ambient air quality guidelines for particulate matter pollution, which has the potential for toxicity, including renal toxicity.
